speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I see you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, frequent falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been progressing, and have they been getting worse gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)

The acute onset of severe right leg weakness and unsteady gait over just one week, combined with a subacute progression of dementia and behavioral changes over six months, is highly suggestive of a prion disease. I need to confirm this with specific testing.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (looking for periodic sharp wave complexes)
REQUEST TEST: CSF analysis (looking for 14-3-3 protein and RT-QuIC)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (looking for cortical ribboning or basal ganglia hyperintensity)
